主要内容: In 2017, store closures significantly impacted the U.S. retail sector, with nearly 7,000 store closure announcements made, a 200% increase from the previous year. FGRT, a retail tracker, reported that many of these closures were still in the planning stages, with some companies targeting closures as far out as 2020. Retailers such as Charming Charlie, Perfumania, Crocs, and GameStop were among those affected, though some closures had not yet occurred. Ascena Retail Group, which owns brands like Dressbarn, Loft, and Ann Taylor, could close up to 667 stores by mid-2019. Meanwhile, landlords like Simon Property Group have taken a more assertive stance, as seen in a recent court ruling that blocked Starbucks from closing all its Teavana stores. This decision has been welcomed by retail real estate investment trusts (REITs), which may use it as a precedent to prevent further store closures. However, some restructuring advisors are pushing for more abrupt closures to minimize negotiation room. Retailers like Gap, J.Crew, and H&M are also planning to close some locations in the coming years. Department store chains such as Macy's, J.C. Penney, and Sears faced challenges during the post-holiday shopping season due to store closures, which led to a decline in retail stocks. Despite the closures, some retailers are still opening new stores, though the number of openings has not been as significant as the closures. In 2017, store closures significantly impacted the retail sector in the US, and the trend is expected to continue in 2018. According to FGRT, the fastest-growing retailers include Dollar General, Dollar Tree, Aldi, and TJX, which owns TJ Maxx and HomeGoods. Meanwhile, beauty retailers Ulta and Sephora are expanding their presence, while companies like Target, Nordstrom, and Forever 21 are also opening more stores, though often in smaller formats. The S&P 500 Retail ETF (XRT) is recovering from previous losses as Wall Street anticipates fourth-quarter earnings, which will include key holiday sales data and further store closure announcements. The retail sector is showing signs of positive trends, with continued expansion and strategic store openings.
